items.excerpt: ## NSA Claims “Temporary Degradation” Behind Outage of Classified Internal Network Nov 18, 2026 The National Security Agency — the largest spy agency in the U.S. — says a “temporary degradation” is behind an outage of its classified internal network. The network, known as NSANet, has been down since at least early Tuesday morning, and some NSA staff have been unable to access their workplace systems, prompting the agency to stagger arrival times for personnel. U.S. officials tell CBS News that so far there is no evidence of a cyberattack. ## Apple and Google Hit by Widespread Service Outages Nov 18, 2026 Apple on Tuesday confirmed widespread service outages on many of its iPhone apps, including Apple Pay and iCloud. Meanwhile, thousands of Gmail users reported disruptions that Google later said were not related to any broad internal system interruptions. This comes amidst a series of other disruptions to air travel, banking and technology infrastructure, including a massive outage at Microsoft last week that disrupted communication for millions of people across at least 74 countries. ... ## Alaska’s Former Democratic Congressmember Peltola Defeats Incumbent GOP Senator Sullivan Nov 18, 2026 In Alaska, former Democratic Congressmember Mary Peltola has defeated incumbent Republican Senator Dan Sullivan. Peltola becomes the first Indigenous woman from Alaska elected to the U.S. Senate. She won with 50.1% of the vote to Sullivan’s 45.8%. Her win brings the Democratic majority in the Senate to 56 seats.

items.excerpt: ## Trump plans to meet separately with Putin on his China trip in addition to their 3-way talks with Xi SHENZHEN, China (AP) — A U.S. official says President Donald Trump plans to meet separately with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday in China, in addition to their already scheduled three-way meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Trump’s meeting with Putin would be the first time the leaders have held talks since their discussions last year in Alaska that failed to broker a deal to ease Russia’s war in Ukraine. Trump is now in China after a visit to the Philippines. He's seeking to reinforce America's status as the world’s leading technology power, but a series of technical outages back home has left his administration scrambling to calm the U.S. public. ## Democrat Hakeem Jeffries is nominated to become House speaker, a historic first WASHINGTON (AP) — Democrats have nominated Hakeem Jeffries to be speaker of the House. The New York congressman has brushed past skeptics and is on track to make history as the nation’s first Black lawmaker with the speaker's gavel. Jeffries secured the nod Wednesday during closed-door voting, 251-11, ahead of a full House vote when the new Congress convenes in January. He ran unopposed. Among those voting no were a group of progressive newcomers, who say there's “still work to be done” to ensure their priorities. Jeffries leads a restive party eager for a change after voters ousted Republicans in a rebuke of President Donald Trump. ... ## Iran widens Gulf attacks by targeting a US air base in Kuwait and sites in Bahrain CAIRO (AP) — Iran has widened its attacks on Gulf neighbors by targeting a U.S. air base in Kuwait following American strikes on an Iranian missile site. Kuwait said Wednesday that its defenses intercepted drones while Bahrain issued two shelter alerts. Saudi Arabia also intercepted a cruise missile fired by Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen following Saudi-led airstrikes that the Houthis say killed at least 17 people. The attacks raise fears of escalation as Iran faces mounting economic pressure from a U.S. naval blockade and continued military confrontation over the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Fed minutes October 2026: Officials expect more rate hikes, worry about AI
items.excerpt: Published Wed, Nov 18 2026 2:00 PM EST Updated An Hour Ago ... Federal Reserve officials expressed confidence in October that further interest rate increases will be needed to stem inflation, though they decided to hold off while gathering more information, according to meeting minutes released Wednesday. Policymakers put artificial intelligence at the core of their discussions, indicating that demand associated with the technology would be "a material source of inflation risk." More broadly, officials said "inflation pressures in the economy were broad based" and would warrant action, with "some" policymakers advocating for a quarter percentage point hike at the meeting. A couple of participants even noted the possibility that a larger increase might be needed at the next policy meeting in December. The meeting summary said "almost all participants judged that, under their baseline outlooks for inflation and the labor market, further action to raise the target range for the federal funds rate … would likely be appropriate, in order to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent objective." In a CNBC interview Wednesday, Fed Governor Christopher Waller reiterated his belief that the Federal Open Market Committee should consider a half-point hike in December. ## AI concern Officials at the meeting expressed a high level of concern over AI, both as a source of inflation and financial instability. Fed staff members who briefed participants noted "that off-balance-sheet leasing commitments and circular financing arrangements among AI-related firms could amplify losses if returns on AI investment were to disappoint." "Most participants observed that AI-related debt had grown rapidly and that much of this growth had taken place through complex and opaque financing structures," the minutes said. "A few participants remarked that AI-related exposures were becoming increasingly concentrated among a small number of firms." Officials said they still expect inflation to fall off sharply in 2027 and beyond as the impact from the current shocks wear off. Ultimately, the FOMC voted 10-2 to keep its benchmark overnight borrowing rate locked in a range between 3.75%-4%. Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Those voting in favor of the hold "pointed to benefits in accumulating additional information, which would help in determining the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee's 2 percent goal." Since the meeting, the inflation data has shown that the pace of price increases remains well above target. The consumer price index in October rose 0.4% for all items and 0.3% for the core that excludes food and energy. Both readings were 0.1 percentage point higher than expected. While indicating concern over how stubborn inflation has been, most Fed officials who have spoken publicly advocated a patient approach. ... At the core of policymakers' concern is whether rising prices related to the Iran war and President Donald Trump's tariffs, in many cases temporary events that wouldn't prompt a response, are instead becoming more entrenched. Markets are fully pricing in a quarter percentage point hike at the Dec. 8-9 meeting that includes low odds of a half-point move, according to the CME Group's FedWatch gauge. Futures traders also are pricing a solid likelihood of two more increases in 2027.

items.title: Economic commentary: Inflation broadens as AI investment risk rises |
items.excerpt: November 18, 2026 ... ## Inflation broadens beyond energy prices Inflation readings for September and October were generally stronger than expected. Headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation rose 0.6% in September, driven in large part by a 9.1% increase in gasoline prices, and that was followed by a stronger than expected 0.4% increase in October, bringing the year-over-year reading to 3.9%. The increases have been broad-based, with no major category registering a decline. Core CPI rose 0.3% in both months. This was the third straight month of a 0.3% reading for core CPI, and the three-month pace at 3.7% annualized is the highest since April 2024. The Producer Price Index (PPI) has also firmed, pushing its year over year increase to the highest level since 2022. Energy prices, particularly diesel, remain the primary driver of producer price pressures. The Fed is concerned that inflation is broadening, and these recent reports do not alleviate that concern. The Fed’s preferred inflation measure, core Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE), increased 0.3% in September, lifting the year-over-year rate to 3.1% from 3.0%. The three-month annualized trend accelerated to 2.9%, up from 2.2% in August and 2.6% a year earlier. The inflation outlook remains vulnerable to higher energy prices and fiscal pressures. The surge in diesel prices represents the primary upside risk to inflation, as higher fuel and freight costs can feed into core inflation by raising the cost of producing and transporting consumer goods. An increasing share of small businesses also plans to raise prices, citing inflation as the primary reason. The energy shock is entirely exogenous and, in its economic impact, is akin to a tax increase. The implication of Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s monetary policy stance is that demand destruction may be the only available transmission channel for bringing inflation back to the Fed’s 2% target unless oil prices decline rapidly. Because current inflationary pressures are fundamentally supply-driven rather than demand-driven, higher interest rates can counter them primarily by weakening demand enough to offset the loss of supply. ## Strong GDP growth, strained consumers The initial estimate of third quarter GDP showed a strong 3.4% annualized increase, up from 2.2% in the second quarter. On a year-over-year basis, however, GDP growth was 2.1%, down slightly from 2.2% in second quarter. - AI-related business investment remained a major engine of growth - Consumer spending proved resilient - Productivity increased at a robust 3.6% annualized pace - Unit labor costs declined at a 0.7% annualized rate Real final sales to private domestic purchasers, a measure of consumer spending and gross private fixed investment, increased 4.9%, marking the strongest quarterly reading since second quarter 2021. Looking ahead, election-driven constraints on data center investment represent a meaningful macroeconomic risk, given that AI investment has been the primary driver of economic growth over the past several years. The September personal income and spending report once again highlighted growing pressure on consumers. Real consumer spending was flat for the first time since January, although it remained up 2.5% year over year. On the income side, real disposable personal income declined 0.3% during the month, bringing its year-over-year growth rate to just 1.0%. With income growing at less than half the pace of spending, the personal saving rate declined to 3.8% from 4.0%, matching its lowest level in the past three years. Consumer spending remains uneven and disproportionately supported by higher-income households. The squeeze on real incomes from higher energy prices is likely to increasingly weigh on lower-income consumers, who devote a disproportionate share of their budgets to energy. Despite the strong third quarter GDP reading, September’s personal income and spending data suggest a considerably weaker handoff into the fourth quarter. ... items.title: Fed’s Barr says rate rises likely lie ahead for economy By Reuters
items.excerpt: NEW YORK, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr said Wednesday he’s likely to be on board with tighter monetary policy in an economy still beset by inflation pressures. “If the economy evolves as I currently forecast, I expect it will be appropriate to raise rates further,” Barr said in the text of remarks prepared for delivery before a conference at the New York Fed. “Inflation is too high, making it hard for American families to make ends meet. Many families are struggling” under the weight of price pressures, Barr said. The official also noted that while inflation is an issue, the economy is otherwise doing well. “The economy is strong, with low unemployment, solid consumer spending, and robust business investment,” Barr said. The Fed’s interest-rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee is scheduled to meet on December 8 and 9.

items.title: Oil prices fall as higher U.S. crude stocks temper supply risks
items.excerpt: Oil prices fell ⁠more than 2% on Wednesday after US crude and fuel inventories posted larger-than-expected rises, according to the Energy Information Administration, adding to expectations of a supply surplus. Brent crude futures shed $2.03, or 2.2%, ​to hit $91.11 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate futures fell $3.82, ​or 4.4%, to $82.19. Spot Brent fell more than $2 a barrel during the session, while WTI lost more than $4. U.S. crude inventories rose by 3.4 million barrels to 417.8 million barrels in the week ended November 13, the EIA said, compared with analysts' expectations in a Reuters poll for a rise of 58,000 barrels. U.S. gasoline stocks rose by ⁠5.2 million ‌barrels in the week to 215.9 million barrels, the EIA said, compared with analysts' expectations ⁠in a Reuters poll for a build of 1.6 million barrels. Distillate stockpiles, which include diesel and heating oil, rose by 1.6 million barrels in the week to 104.9 million barrels, versus expectations for a rise of 1.3 million barrels, the EIA data showed.

items.title: U.S. Firms’ Year-Ahead Inflation Expectations Rise to 2.5% in November | TokenPost
items.excerpt: U.S. businesses’ expectations for inflation over the coming year rose to 2.5% in November, while a separate measure of expected unit costs remained above its prepandemic average. The year-ahead business inflation expectation increased from 2.3% in October, a rise of 0.2 percentage point. The unit-cost measure stayed above its 2.0% prepandemic average. The 2.5% reading is for business inflation expectations; the 2.0% figure is the prepandemic average for unit-cost expectations. The November results were released Wednesday, Nov. 18.

items.title: Reuters Entertainment News Summary | International
items.excerpt: Reuters | Updated: 18-11-2026 18:26 IST | Created: 18-11-2026 18:26 IST ### Key Takeaways Following is a summary of current entertainment news briefs. Amazon's Bezos says he helped pick Pattinson as Bond Amazon founder and chairman Jeff Bezos said he was heavily involved in selecting "Batman" actor Robert Pattinson to take on the iconic film role ​of James Bond. Bezos spoke at Semafor's Silicon Valley & The World conference on Tuesday, a day after the company announced Pattinson as the next 007. He said ​Amazon narrowed down a larger group and screen-tested five actors by having them perform three scenes in full costume ‌on sets. Skydance ​names film chiefs for Paramount, Warner Bros labels Skydance named Don Granger and Kira Goldberg presidents of the Motion Picture Group at Paramount Pictures, while promoting Jesse Ehrman to president of the Motion Picture Group at Warner Bros Pictures, outlining the leadership structure for its combined film business. The changes come as Skydance seeks to build a company capable of delivering 30 films a year, with Paramount Pictures and Warner Bros Pictures retaining separate identities and distinct creative mandates, according to an internal memo to staff on Tuesday from Skydance ‌Motion Picture Group co-chairs Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein. Raye and Rosalia lead nominations for music's Grammy Awards British singer Raye, the artist behind the genre-mixing hit that asks "Where Is My Husband!," landed at the top of the list of Grammy Award nominees on Monday, ahead of Spanish musician Rosalia and "Choosin' Texas" artist Ella Langley. Raye earned 11 Grammy nominations including nods for song and record of the year for "Husband," and for album of the year for "This Music May Contain Hope." Rosalia racked up nine nominations, days after she dominated the Latin Grammys with her album "Lux." Disney tops earnings estimates on theme park, NFL strength; to boost content spend Walt Disney exceeded Wall Street expectations for quarterly revenue and earnings on Tuesday, as higher theme park attendance and strong NFL ‌viewership lifted results, and said it planned to increase content spending by 9% next fiscal year. The owner of the Disney+ streaming service and ESPN cable network said it would boost cash content spending to $26 billion next year, including by investing more in international programming and sports rights. British actor Robert Pattinson named as new James Bond British actor Robert ‌Pattinson will be the next James Bond, Amazon MGM Studios announced on Monday, taking on one of cinema's most coveted roles. The Bond franchise — about a British secret agent known for his charm, his tailored tuxedos and a fondness for martinis "shaken, not stirred" — is among the longest-running and highest-grossing in Hollywood history. UK authorities investigating after Russell Brand's message from prison British authorities are investigating whether Russell Brand, the comedian found guilty of rape, has broken rules which ban prisoners from making statements that can cause distress to victims, the Prime Minister's spokesperson said on Monday. Prime Minister Andy Burnham's spokesperson was asked about comments made by Brand's wife Laura on a YouTube podcast, during which she read out a statement from him saying he was innocent. Harry Styles, Billie Eilish and Cher to headline UK's Glastonbury in 2027 Harry Styles, Sam Fender, Billie Eilish and Cher will headline Britain's Glastonbury next year, the organisers ⁠said on their website on ​Wednesday, as the sold-out festival returns after taking a year off in 2026. British singer Harry Styles, who ⁠recently completed a 30-show residency at Madison Square Garden in New York, will play the festival for the first time, while Cher will take the legends slot at the age of 81. Britain's Prince William visits Bollywood studio, watches dancers Britain's Prince William watched Bollywood dances and toured a film studio in Mumbai on the last day of his royal visit to India on Wednesday, while his wife, Kate Middleton, spoke to health workers ⁠at a maternity hospital in the city. The royal couple, who are on a three-day visit to India's financial capital, will end their trip in New Delhi and meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi late on Wednesday.
